summary: N1 near-duplicates: a telemetry frame decoder with sixteen cloned functions (ten input decoders that differ only in the cell offset, six config setters that differ only in the struct member). v2 changes the range limit of exactly one decoder; v3 only reorders definitions, swapping neighbouring clones so that each lands on a sibling's former address.

pairs.intent: Exactly one of the sixteen cloned functions changes: fr_dec_ain6 tightens its upper limit from 1000 to 900. The other nine decoders and six setters are text-identical and share one CFG with it, so a matcher that works from shape or hash has many equally good partners for the changed function and near-perfect false partners for every unchanged one.

pairs.intent: Nothing changes except the order of the definitions. Neighbouring clones swap places (ain0<->ain1, ain2<->ain3, ..., set_gain<->set_offset, ...) and, because the clones compile to the same size, each one now sits at the address its sibling had in v2. Position or address based pairing is wrong for every clone.
